key_insight: Projecting reconstructed penalty-gradient states onto a known ball preserves Byzantine resilience under compressed federated-learning uploads.
engineering_relevance: The framework reduces communication while preventing malicious clients from accumulating unbounded server-side states through compressed updates.
method: Honest workers upload compressed penalty-gradient residuals; the server projects each reconstructed state.
FRPG-CS uses consistent sparsification with fresh reserve rows; LAG-FRPG triggers uploads only when needed.
For smooth, strongly convex losses, analysis separates compressor-independent Byzantine error from faster-decaying compression error.
evidence_signal: On MNIST and Fashion-MNIST under the Min-Max attack, the proposed algorithms achieved the highest accuracy among twelve methods.
watch_item: The methods are not universally best: a compressed-momentum benchmark led in attack-free accuracy, and a local-update benchmark used less total traffic.
paper_title: Projected Penalty-Gradient Tracking for Communication-Efficient Byzantine-Resilient Federated Learning
